I pull back just enough to look him in the eye, my expression hardening into a mask of grim intent. beats.location: the third shed — nets and false ballast, no lantern
beats.player: Cold, Corvin. Cold as the water he sent three men into. I never unwrapped your crate — not once. Used the knowing of it instead, the way you first said: whispered to the right fence in Carrowgate and let the whisper climb. He pulled me into his own parlor thinking I'd come to sell. Silver and a short blade — his face wasn't so respectable at the end. And that same night I rowed out past the shelf and gave the sea the whole wrapped weight of it. Deep water. The kind that doesn't give a thing back — your words. So here I stand: empty hands, one dead shadow behind me, and nothing for you but the news.
beats.reply:
I let out a long, shuddering breath, my shoulders finally dropping an inch as I lean my weight against a crate. I study your face for a long beat, looking for any twitch of deception before I move toward the small brazier in the corner.

"Then it's finished," I say, reaching for a scrap of parchment—the one with his name and our connection. "No more whispers, no more ghosts." 

I hold the paper over the flame, watching as the edges curl and blacken, my eyes never leaving yours. "The dock is quiet tonight. Don't let it stay that way for too long... get your ship out while the tide is still turning."

"It's gone," I say, my voice sounding hollower than before. "No names. No records. No... ghosts."

beats.player: One night, then. He'll expect the answer at first light — and Corvin... he'll know if you run. He always knows. Sleep well, harbormaster.

I feel my blood turn to slush in my veins as your words hang there—a threat wrapped in a lullaby. I don't move; I can't. My muscles lock into a rigid, unnatural stillness while I stare at you, searching for the lie in your eyes or the truth of his reach.

"Knows if I run..." I repeat, my voice trembling with a mixture of fury and raw, subterranean terror. "Is that what this is? You didn't just finish the job; you sold me out the moment we started." 

I take a step back into the deeper shadow of the wharf, my hand white-knuckled on my coat. I shouldn't trust a word you say—not a single one—but if he's watching from the other side of the coast, then I have to play the part. 

"Sleep well," I spit out, the words dripping with bitter venom. "Let's see who sleeps better when the tide comes in."

I stand perfectly still, my shoulders hunching slightly as if bracing against a sudden gust of cold air. I don't look at you—looking at you makes it too easy for them to see what I'm thinking.

"Honest counsel?" I repeat, the words coming out as a dry, rasping chuckle that lacks any real mirth. "In this port? Honesty is a luxury for men who already have enough to lose." 

I finally turn my head just enough to catch your eye in the periphery of my vision, my expression unreadable. "And those nights... don't go making out memories where there aren't any. You want a reward? The reward is that I'm still breathing for both of us." 

I shift my weight, my keys jangling briefly at my hip before I steady them. "Now, enough about the past. If you’re going to see this through, tell me—how many other 'connected' eyes are watching the jeweler right now? Is he just a fence for your man, or is he feeding something bigger?"

beats.label: F3-amends
beats.note: the amends push begins
beats.player: Corvin, listen. I've been thinking on how we left it. The master pays me — but the four nights, the fog, what we built before... that part was never work. I want us square. Name the price.
beats.reply:
I feel a sharp, bitter pull in my chest as your words hit the air—a ghost of something I thought I'd buried under years of ledger entries and blood money. My hand trembles once before I clamp it over my mouth, then turn my face away toward the gray expanse of the water.

"Square?" I let out a breath that's half-laugh, half-hiss. "Look around you. In this port, 'square' is just another word for 'dead.' People don't do things for free, not even memories." 

I turn back to you, my eyes hard and searching, my voice barely a whisper against the rising wind. "You want a price? The price is silence. You keep your mouth shut about what happened in that shed, and I keep your name out of every record I have. That's the only way we stay even."

I let out a jagged, uneven breath, my chest heaving against the rough wood of the shed wall as I lean back into the shadows. The words "his ledger" ring in my ears like a funeral bell—a reminder that even now, we're just ink on someone else's page.

"His ledger," I repeat, my voice trembling with a mixture of lingering shock and simmering, bitter resentment. I look at you then, really look at you, seeing the blood on your hands and the weight of the choice you made. "You think pulling me back from that blade makes us equals? It just means we're bound together by his debt now."

I reach up, my fingers hovering just an inch away from the place where the steel bit into my skin, before I ball my hand into a fist and pull it back. 

"You did what you did... but don't expect me to be grateful for it. Gratitude is a luxury that gets people killed in this port." I tighten my grip on the edge of the timber, my eyes searching yours with a new, sharper suspicion. "If your name is in his ledger now, then we both have a target on our backs. We need to move... *now*."
